chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) used to whip the free man, the slave, the Jew, and the Christian for wine and the intoxicant al-Nabeez, eighty (lashes). So it was said, 'What is the matter with the Jew and the Christian?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'When they display that openly in a city from the cities, because it is not for them that they should be displaying (it openly).'
Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ja'far ibn Rizqallah or a man from Ja'far ibn Rizqallah who said:

A Christian man was brought before Al-Mutawakkal who had committed fornication with a Muslim woman, so he wanted to establish the Hadd penalty upon him, but he became a Muslim. So Yahya ibn Aktham said, 'His faith has demolished his polytheism and his deed.' And some of them said, 'Whip him with three Hadd penalties,' and some of them said, 'Do with him such and such.'

So Al-Mutawakkal ordered a letter to be sent to Abu al-Hasan al-Thani (peace be upon him) asking him about that. So when he read the letter, he wrote: 'He is whipped until he dies.' But Yahya ibn Aktham disagreed, and the jurists of al-Askar disagreed with that, and they said, 'O Commander of the Faithful, ask about this, for it is a thing which the Book does not speak of and a Sunnah has not come with it.'

So he wrote to him that the jurists of the Muslims had disagreed with this and said, 'A Sunnah has not come with it, and the Book does not speak of it. Therefore, explain to us why you made whipping until death obligatory upon him.'

In the Name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. [40:84] When they saw Our Punishment, they said: 'We believe in Allah alone and we deny what we used to associate with Him.' [40:85] But their belief was not going to profit them when they had seen Our Punishment; (this is) Allah's Way, which has been customary regarding His servants, and there the unbelievers are in loss.
He (the narrator) said, 'So Al-Mutawakkal ordered by it, and he was whipped until he died.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Imam Ali, peace be upon him)
key_terms.أَهْلُ الزِّمَّةِ: People under responsibility (non-Muslims in Islamic state)
key_terms.النَّبِيذِ: Nabeez (an intoxicant made from dates or grapes)

ai.seo_question: What is the Hadd penalty for non-Muslims drinking wine and the ruling on a convert avoiding punishment?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes the principle of equality in Hadd penalties for Ahl al-Zimma, noting that their punishment is contingent upon public display of the act, reflecting the juristic view that their private lives are less regulated. The narrative regarding the Christian convert under Caliph al-Mu'tasim highlights a significant Shia legal debate on whether conversion nullifies the specific Hadd for non-Muslims or merely adds to it, with Imam al-Hadi (AS) citing Surah Ghafir to justify the 'whipping until death' ruling based on the 'Way of Allah' (Sunnat Allah) for those who delay faith until seeing punishment. This incident underscores the authority of the Imams in interpreting divine precedent for judicial application during the Abbasid era.
